title: Count Triplets with Equal Distinct Counts

reported.text: Count triplets (i,j,k) where s[i..j] and s[j+1..k] have the same number of distinct characters (set -> bitmask -> binary search).

sources.passage:
Google L3 Onsite Interview Question
I recently gave Google Onsite Interview and I was asked this question. Was able to give the brute force solution using set and then gave the optimized solution using BitMask.


But the interviewer said there is another efficient approach apart from bitmask.


He gave me hints and I was able to figure out that I have to use Binary Search but couldn't come up with how to apply binary search.


Can anyone help to provide the solution?


What do you think my outcome would be for this interview? (in terms of Hire, Leaning Hire etc.)


You have been given a string s. Two strings s1 and s2 are considered to be magical string pairs if the number of distinct characters in s1 is equal to s2. Given a string s, find the number of triplets i, j, k which satisfy this condition. The string s1 is from s[i, j] and s2 from [j+1, k].

reported.text: RPC logs {id, timestamp, in/out} with a timeout: find the first time any RPC expires.

sources.passage:
Google | L3 | All rounds
Recently I appeared for Google interviews, I was approached by recruiter on linkedin. Here are the questions I was asked in all rounds :

Round 1
We have logs printing when RPC come in and go out in format {RPC_ID, Timestamp, Type(in/out)} and a timeout time. Timeout time means after RPC has come in, it will expire after this timeout time if it has not gone out. Find the first time when any RPC will expire.

Round 2
You are given array of array in which each array represents a neighbourhood with house number. You have to rearrange houses in such a way houses in each neighbourhood is sorted, each neighbourhood size is maintained and no neighbourhood has duplicate house numbers. There can be same house number houses in multiple neighbourhood.

Round 3
Given a matrix (not necessarily a square) of size m cross n of 1s and 0s, find a square a 1s in it. Return the top left index and length of side of the square, return 0 if there is no square in the matrix. It is given than square's side is of length atleast sqrt(n).

Round 4
Given an array of positive numbers, find a subarray of size>1 with maximum min plus max value in that subarray.

There is an array arr of wind speeds on each day, a sailor has some power K
K reduces by 1 if he sails on a day and he covers arr[I] distance on that day, if he does not sail on that day distance covered is 0 and K increases by 1. Find the maximum distance\xA0he\xA0can\xA0travel.

Round 5 (Googliness)
Cancelled as I did not perform well in above rounds

title: Satellite Grid: Island then Enclosed Lakes

reported.text: Satellite image grid of land 'X' and water '.', with a given coordinate: find the island (BFS flood fill), then identify/count lakes enclosed by that island.

sources.passage:
Google L4 Interview Experience Date October 5th 2026
# Google L4 SWE Interview Experience — Rejected After Technical and Googliness Rounds (October 2026)

Hi everyone,

I wanted to share my recent Google L4 SWE interview experience and get some feedback from the community.

### Interview Timeline

- **September 2026:** Connected with a recruiter for an L4 SWE position.
- Completed the GHA and coding assessment and was shortlisted.
- **October 5, 2026:** Attended the virtual technical and Googliness interviews.
- **Final result:** Rejected.

### Technical Interview — Grid / BFS / Flood Fill

The problem involved a satellite image represented as an `N × M` grid, where:

- `X` represents land/islands.
- `.` represents water.
- A coordinate `(r, c)` is provided.

**Part 1:** I proposed a BFS approach similar to Number of Islands. The interviewer confirmed that my approach was correct and asked me to implement it. I completed the code.

**Part 2:** The follow-up was related to identifying/counting lakes enclosed by islands.

I found the follow-up question difficult to understand. I asked for clarification multiple times, but the interviewer mostly nodded and repeated the explanation in a similar way. I didn't receive any specific hints that helped clarify what was expected.

Based on my understanding, I proposed checking for lakes while traversing the islands using BFS.

The interviewer said, **"Yes, we can also do it that way,"** but mentioned that there was no need to implement the code and moved to the Q&A portion.

I later realized that the problem may have involved a boundary-based flood-fill approach, although I'm still not completely sure what the interviewer expected.

### Googliness Round

I was asked standard behavioral questions with follow-ups.

One question I struggled with was:

**"If a project is unclear or there is ambiguity, how would you handle it?"**

I couldn't structure my response properly. I stumbled over my words and went in a different direction instead of answering the question clearly.

I recognize that I could have communicated my approach better in this round.

### Final Feedback

Unfortunately, I received a rejection.

The recruiter mentioned that I needed to **strengthen my technical concepts and practice more LeetCode problems**.

### My Thoughts

title: Split a/b String Fairly with Two Cuts

reported.text: String of 'a' and 'b' with even counts of each; make at most 2 cuts and distribute pieces between Alice and Bob so both get equal a's and equal b's. Return the cut indices.

sources.passage:
Google India L3 || Interview Experience || Offer Accepted
Hey Everyone, Im sharing my recent Google Software Engineer L3 interview experience. 
The LeetCode Discuss section helped me a lot in my prep and its time for me to give back to the community.

There were total 4 Interviews.
1. Virtual Technical round
2. Virtual googliness round
3. Onsite Technical round
4. Onsite Technical round


---


**Virtual Technical Round**
Question: A variation of [https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-good-subarray-sum](https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-good-subarray-sum) in which we have to return any pair of indices {i, j} rather than the max sum.

---


**Virtual Googliness Round**
Simple behavioural and hypothetical questions.

---
**Onsite Technical Rounds**
Both the rounds were on the same day, back to back in Google's office.
Two different interviewers and two different questions.

Question1: 
It was a story wrapped question but the crux of the questions was,
Given a string consisting of only 2 letters 'a' and 'b' such that the number of 'a' and number of 'b' is even in the string. You can make at most 2 cuts in the string and divide the sub-strings amongst Alice and Bob in such a way that the number of 'a' Alice has == number of 'a' bob has and number of 'b' Alice has == number of 'b' bob has. Return the index or indices of the cut(s).

Question2:
Another story wrapped question but the crux was,
Given an array of integers in one operation you will select any element from the array and remove it from the array then you have to tell that is it possible to divide that new array into two subarrays such that the sum of the subarrays is equal (after doing the operation).




---

I was able to solve every question and was give a positive verdict in each round. (Was told to work on my time management as a feedback)
After completing all the rounds my recruiter called me in 2 days to tell me that I have cleared the interviews and my profile is being sent for team-matching stage, got a team match in 2 business days, had a good talk with the manager. Then came the Hiring Committee, in which my packet was sent to the HC, after 3 days recruiter called for Compensation discussion and on the same day got the offer.


---

If anybody needs some tips on how I did it, I would just say, to believe in yourself because any day your destiny can change and you would want to be ready to
